title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

requirements.stmt: For missing values, use a three-level cascading fallback: intersection matching, then union matching, then global prior.
requirements.quote: We employ a three-level cascading strategy that progressively relaxes the matching criteria when stricter criteria fail to find similar samples.

requirements.stmt: Level 1: if S1(i) is nonempty, estimate missing feature encodings as mean one-hot vectors over samples matching all observed features.

requirements.stmt: Level 2: if no intersection match exists, use the union over samples matching any observed feature.
requirements.quote: When no samples match across all observed features simultaneously, we cannot apply the intersection-based estimation.

requirements.stmt: Level 3: if the union is empty, use the global prior probability over bins for each missing feature.
requirements.quote: When S2(i) = ∅, we cannot leverage local similarity and must use the global distribution of each missing feature.
